Net: not clearly better. The new layout is playable, but every fixed view that looks toward the CBD got worse and the new land is empty.

BLIND GTA V A/B (each pair decided before I checked which side was ours):
- Pair-1: GTAV-09 wins. It has a dramatic chase angle, reflective paint, motion streaks and a layered background. Ours shows flat beige land, rows of one identical tree, an empty road, a plain slab tower and HUD clutter.
- Pair-2: GTAV-15 wins. It shows a dense, believable city of roofs and greenery with deep haze. Ours shows a grid of empty paved plots with tree dots and stubby cylinders; only the water holds up.
- Pair-3: GTAV-05 wins. It has cars, police, pedestrians, shopfronts and signage. Ours is an empty junction with no buildings, cars or people.
- Pair-4: GTAV-20 wins. It has layered terrain and city depth. Ours is washed-out haze over empty plots and untextured box towers.
Verdict: OURS LOSES 4/4. Wowed: no.. Singapore: FAILS for the new downtown.

What is right:
- The basic geography: the bay basin and river-mouth shape, low bridges over the water, granite-coped seawalls with railings, rain-tree boulevards.
- Left-hand traffic, double yellow kerb lines and real road-name signs (Fullerton Road, Raffles Avenue).
- An NS Square float with a helipad.

Why it still fails:
- Against CONCEPT-03 (helicopter view with shophouse roofs, the river, the Esplanade dome, a wall of CBD towers behind MBS and dense HDB) and CONCEPT-02 (a boulevard with dense frontage and skyline), the downtown reads as an unbuilt planning layout.
- None of the Fullerton, the Esplanade 'durians', the Boat Quay shophouses, the Raffles Place towers or the Helix exist in this build. Those belong to separate pieces.
- What you see instead is beige or grass plots in a regular grid, one repeated umbrella-tree model in rigid rows, and no people or cars.
- The only things that say Singapore are the inherited MBS, Flyer, ArtScience and Merlion. They are still in their pre-move, mirrored positions, and the CBD skyline that used to sell Singapore in the bay views is now thinner.
- The NS Square pad is dressed with the aviation compound's AVTURJET fuel truck and windsock, so it reads as an airfield rather than a civic waterfront (/private/tmp/opus55/critic/downtown-map-M1/review/fly_walk_ns_square.jpg).

Judge: The commercial game wins all four pairs clearly (1: A, 2: A, 3: A, 4: B), and none was close to indistinguishable. The judging was not truly blind: every commercial frame carries a GTA V logo, and every in-development frame except pair 4 shows a gameplay HUD. The reference frames are also staged promotional shots with grading, while the dev frames are raw gameplay captures. The verdicts rest on content, though, and would hold without the logo or HUD. The in-development game's real strengths are its sky and cloud dome, warm sun and bloom, and recognisable landmark silhouettes (triple-tower hotel, Ferris wheel, bay). Its failures repeat across every pair. (1) The world is empty: no traffic, no pedestrians, and only one boat in four frames. (2) Open space is placeholder: vast flat brown paved slabs with a perfectly regular grid of planter squares (pairs 2 and 4), or empty plazas where a downtown street wall should be (pair 3). (3) One umbrella-tree model is repeated at fixed spacing everywhere. (4) Buildings are boxes with flat window-grid textures and no relief. (5) Lighting has no value structure: the haze washes frames out instead of separating dark foregrounds from bright distances, and the dev game has no counterpart to the reference's hero subjects with strong material response (chrome, glossy paint, rotor blur). The highest-leverage fixes, in order: populate streets with traffic and people, replace the gridded plazas with dense, varied city blocks, add tree and building variety, and give aerial and vista frames a contrasty foreground and a proper backlit falloff. Only two frames genuinely wowed: the reference helicopter-over-downtown shot (pair 2 A) and the hillside-sign golden-hour vista (pair 4 B). No dev frame did.
